name: Orlyata Rossii ("Eaglets of Russia") / Орлята России

name: Krympatriotcentr (Crimea Patriot Centre) / Крымпатриотцентр

notes: Director S. O. Havrylchuk was sentenced in absentia in Ukraine to 12 years (May 2025); the centre coordinates the Avangard network in Crimea.

notes: Training takes place at an active Russian military unit; head K. S. Miroshnychenko.

name: Voin ("Warrior") centre / Центр «Воин»
category: Youth movement or federal structure
type: State network of military-sports training centres
affiliation: Rospatriotcentr / Russian Union of Martial Arts (Kiriyenko, Trutnev); approved by Putin in September 2022
territory: Kherson, Zaporizhzhia, Luhansk and Donetsk oblasts
legal_status: Autonomous non-profit organisation: Voin Centre for Special Training, Sports and Military-Patriotic Education
activity: Preparation for service in the Russian armed forces, ages 14 to 18 (extended programme 19 to 35); coordinates with the Luhansk Cossack Cadet Corps
participants: Not stated for the occupied territories as a whole; at least 70 students at the first camp (Henichesk). Summer sessions across Russia: 10,905 cadets in 2024 and 12,935 in 78 sessions in 2025. From the occupied territories: over 300 children from Donetsk, Luhansk, Zaporizhzhia and Kherson oblasts in a single 2024 session; 781 from the "DNR" and over 140 from the "LNR" in one 2025 session; at least 91 from Zaporizhzhia oblast and 123 from Luhansk oblast confirmed in two documented 2026 groups
sources: https://crvsp.ru/center; https://lb.ua/blog/koalitsiia_ua5am/620037_voini_rosiyskogo_rezhimu_yak.html; https://war-sanctions.gur.gov.ua/kidnappers/companies/13074; https://1news.zp.ua/; Centre for the Study of Occupation study of the Voin summer network, Mariupol monitoring, August 2026
notes: Director I. V. Kazarezov from February 2024; national umbrella structure for the networks in entries 25 to 30. The Avangard defence and sports camp in Volgograd oblast is the main hub for Voin summer sessions: about 2,200 to 2,600 adolescents in 2024, 3,400 in 2025, about 4,500 planned for 2026. Programmes combine drone operation, tactical medicine, engineering, communications, weapons training and security fundamentals.

name: Centre for the Military-Patriotic Education of Students, Sevastopol / «Центр военно-патриотического воспитания учащейся молодежи»

name: Bagira young marines club / ВПК юных морских пехотинцев «Багира»

name: Patriot club, Yevpatoria / ВПК «Патриот» (Євпаторія)

activity: Hand-to-hand combat from age 5, shooting, grenade throwing, disassembling the AK-74, medical training
sources: https://war-sanctions.gur.gov.ua/kidnappers/companies/13689; https://investigator.org.ua/ua/investigations/266111/
notes: Head I. V. Novikov; listed by the Myrotvorets database as a former Wagner Group fighter (not independently verified).

name: Avangard training and methodological centre / «Авангард»
category: Youth movement or federal structure
type: State network of methodological centres for military-patriotic education
affiliation: Initiated by S. Shoigu (former Russian defence minister); network of more than 100 centres across Russia
territory: Crimea (Simferopol / Orikhove village, Kerch, Yevpatoria); Luhansk oblast
address: Office 1, Building 9, Patriot Park, Odintsovo, Moscow oblast, Russia, 143070 (head office)
founded: October 2023 (first camp session in Crimea); April 2024 (agreement with the "LNR")
legal_status: Autonomous non-profit organisation: Avangard Training and Methodological Centre for the Military-Patriotic Education of Youth
activity: Five-day sessions for pupils in years 9 to 11; the Crimean Avangard operates in Kerch through the Sviatohor club and in Yevpatoria through Krympatriotcentr
participants: First session 100 children (October 2023); at least 10 sessions planned for 2024
sources: https://24tv.ua/avangard-voyin-tot-yak-rf-gotuye-ditey-do-viyni-osint-rozsliduvannya_n2998199; https://www.radiosvoboda.org/a/news-rosia-militaryzatsia-molodi-krym/32865216.html; https://war-sanctions.gur.gov.ua/kidnappers/companies/12013; https://militarnyi.com/
notes: A plot of more than 10 hectares was taken from the former Gagarin camp for construction; UK sanctions (FCDO, 19 November 2024, together with Yunarmiya). The Avangard camp in Volgograd oblast, the network's main site for children from the occupied territories, took about 2,200 to 2,600 adolescents in 2024 and 3,400 in 2025, with about 4,500 planned for 2026; the first 2026 session had about 900 cadets and the final August 2026 session about 1,200 from 55 regions (Centre for the Study of Occupation, August 2026).

activity: Pre-conscription training, training of territorial-defence fighters; coordination of the network of military-patriotic clubs in the occupied territories
sources: https://war-sanctions.gur.gov.ua/kidnappers/companies/13989; https://almenda.org/rol-yaltinskogo-oseredku-dtsaaf-u-militarizacii-ditej-na-timchasovo-okupovanij-teritorii/; https://archive.ph/JFMm8; https://www.radiosvoboda.org/a/news-zelensky-sanktsii-artek/33439180.html

name: Rus club, Luhansk oblast / ВПК «Русь»

legal_status: NGO: Rus Regional Youth Military-Patriotic Club
activity: Forming "patriotic consciousness", preparation for military service; annual trips to military field camps in Russia (hostage-rescue combat, knife throwing, weapons assembly)
sources: https://war-sanctions.gur.gov.ua/kidnappers/companies/13861
notes: Curator is an FSB officer; close ties to Russian security structures.

name: Spasaya Detstvo ("Saving Childhood") charitable foundation / БФ «Спасая детство»

territory: Donetsk oblast (origin of the children); transfer to Russia
address: Premises 213, Floor 6, Building 9, Greenwood, Putilkovo, Krasnogorsk, Moscow oblast, Russia, 143440

notes: Cross-tag: Accountability and Legal (forced deportation; the child leaves the territory).

name: Volunteers of Victory all-Russian movement / «Волонтеры Победы»
category: Youth movement or federal structure
affiliation: Rosmolodyozh; joint projects with the Russian Ministry of Science and Russian Railways
locality: Zaporizhzhia oblast (regional branch); Crimea ("Victory Train" project)
legal_status: All-Russian public movement Volunteers of Victory
funding: Federal budget; joint projects with state corporations
activity: School for training volunteer propagandists; a travelling museum train for children designed to create an "emotional connection with the war"
sources: https://almenda.org/finansuvannya-molodizhnoi-politiki-v-rosii/; https://war-sanctions.gur.gov.ua/kidnappers/companies/12014; https://www.gov.uk/government/news/uk-sanctions-actors-forcibly-deporting-indoctrinating-and-militarising-ukrainian-children; https://qirim.news/

name: Military-Patriotic Youth of Good Will, Alupka / «Военно-патриотическая молодёжь доброй воли»

name: Young Sevastopolites / «Юные севастопольцы»

sources: https://investigator.org.ua/ua/investigations/266966/; https://crimea-news.com/society/2024/03/15/1324489.html
notes: In practice an extension of Yunarmiya to pre-school age; the youngest cohort documented in the dataset.

name: Yunarmiya ("Youth Army") / «Юнармия»
category: Youth movement or federal structure
affiliation: Russian Ministry of Defence; co-founder DOSAAF (since 2016)
locality: Network of branches (Crimea, Sevastopol, occupied Donetsk and Luhansk, Zaporizhzhia, Kherson region)
founded: Late 2015 to early 2016 (Putin decree No. 536 of 29 October 2015); Donbas, spring 2019; the other occupied territories, November 2022
legal_status: All-Russian movement subordinate to the Russian Ministry of Defence
funding: State budget: 2024, 270 million roubles directly to Yunarmiya (out of 46 billion roubles for "patriotic education" overall); 2025, about 800 million roubles planned plus 200 million from the Ministry of Defence
activity: Assembling and disassembling Kalashnikov rifles, shooting, drill and tactical training; coordinates clubs (Amazonki, Vityaz), channels members into cadet classes, military colleges and the Voin centre
participants: At least 50,000 in the occupied territories (2024 to 2025): LNR 102 detachments in 24 municipalities, over 6,000 members; DNR over 5,000; Crimea 15,000 (from 1,500 in 2017); Russia-wide about 1.8 million
sources: https://yunarmy.ru/; https://investigator.org.ua/ua/investigations/266966/; Barbieri, Ethnopolitics 23(5), 2024, pp. 515 to 536; Hird et al., ISW, 2024
notes: US sanctions (OFAC, 3 July 2024) and UK sanctions (FCDO, 19 November 2024); head V. Golovin ("Struna") from December 2024, Hero of Russia; on 11 May 2025 Pushilin ordered 100% enrolment of Mariupol schoolchildren.

name: Movement of the First / «Движение первых»
category: Youth movement or federal structure
type: State-public movement of children and youth (all-Russian)
affiliation: Absorbed the Russian Schoolchildren's Movement and Bolshaya Peremena; Orlyata Rossii is its primary-school arm
locality: Mariupol (40 branches in 27 institutions), Zaporizhzhia oblast (190 branches), LNR (about 3,500 detachments)
founded: 2022 (created); December 2022 (first branches in the occupied territories)
legal_status: All-Russian public-state movement of children and youth
activity: Zarnitsa games, meetings with participants in the war, "patronage" of soldiers' families; use of the Z and V symbols and the St George ribbon
participants: Mariupol 1,500 children; Zaporizhzhia oblast 19,000 children; LNR over 70,000 events per school year
sources: https://www.gov.uk/government/news/uk-sanctions-actors-forcibly-deporting-indoctrinating-and-militarising-ukrainian-children; Hird et al., ISW, 2024; McGlynn et al., Capturing the Minds, 2026
notes: UK sanctions, 3 September 2025, together with Volunteers of Victory.

name: Young Guard of United Russia (MGER) / Молодая Гвардия Единой России
category: Youth movement or federal structure
type: Youth wing of the ruling party
affiliation: United Russia party; ideological curator State Duma deputy and GRU officer D. Sablin
territory: Donetsk oblast; branches across the occupied territories
activity: "Patriotic education", volunteering for the Russian army, mounting "Hero's Stars" on the homes of killed occupation soldiers (with Molodaya Respublika); a volunteer company with Boevoe Bratstvo

notes: Head M. Averkin, convicted in absentia in Ukraine.

name: Rospatriotcentr and the Russian Union of Martial Arts / Роспатриотцентр

affiliation: Co-chairs S. Kiriyenko (first deputy head of the Russian presidential administration) and Yu. Trutnev (deputy prime minister); project approved by Putin in September 2022

name: Rosmolodyozh (Federal Agency for Youth Affairs) / Росмолодёжь

sources: https://almenda.org/finansuvannya-molodizhnoi-politiki-v-rosii/
notes: Involved in launching the Yug Molodoy movement (entry 8).

name: Patriot youth centre, Kherson oblast / АНО «Молодежный центр «Патриот»»

type: Youth centre (not to be confused with the Patriot club in Yevpatoria)

name: Redut military-patriotic centre, Luhansk / «Редут»
category: Club, cadet corps or camp inside the territory
affiliation: Luhansk Taras Shevchenko Pedagogical University
activity: Weapons training (mock-ups, VR simulators, laser tag) for students and schoolchildren; linked to the Zachyot forum
sources: Centre for the Study of Occupation monitoring, Luhansk oblast, November 2025
notes: Named after a killed fighter, B. Belhrai.

name: Molodaya Respublika ("Young Republic"), DNR / Молодая Республика
category: Youth movement or federal structure
affiliation: Works with the Young Guard of United Russia
activity: Mounting "Hero's Stars" and memorial stars on the homes of killed participants in the war; involving schoolchildren and students alongside branches of the Movement of the First and Yunarmiya
sources: Centre for the Study of Occupation monitoring, Donetsk oblast, October 2025 and January 2026
notes: Acts jointly with the Boevoe Bratstvo volunteer company (entry 39).

name: Luhansk Character educational programme / «Луганский характер»
category: Curriculum programme
affiliation: Order of the "head of the LNR" L. Pasechnik; delivered through Movement of the First detachments
funding: Budget of the LNR occupation administration
activity: Tiered structure (primary school "September Eaglets", middle school "Pioneers", senior school "Toilers") layered onto Yunarmiya, Znanie and the Movement of the First
participants: About 3,500 detachments (according to the "LNR minister of education" I. Kusov)
sources: Centre for the Study of Occupation monitoring, Luhansk oblast, August to October 2025
notes: Type: curriculum programme; Pasechnik calls it "know-how" and plans to scale it up.

name: Rubikon military field camps and the People's Militia (Narodnaya Druzhina), Donetsk oblast / «Рубикон» и «Народная дружина»
category: Club, cadet corps or camp inside the territory
affiliation: People's Militia (paramilitary formation)
activity: Weapons handling, tactics, combat medicine, drone piloting; instructors described by propaganda as former Ukrainian servicemen
sources: Centre for the Study of Occupation monitoring, Donetsk oblast, October 2025
confidence_note: One-off event, recorded as an activity of the People's Militia rather than a separate organisation
notes: Example of a one-off event; the People's Militia itself is to be assessed separately against the recurring-presence criterion.

name: Komsomol (revived), Mariupol / «Комсомол»
category: Youth movement or federal structure
affiliation: Local occupation administration
activity: Clean-ups, painting monuments, raising the red flag, the "Return Lenin to Mariupol" campaign (June 2025)
sources: Centre for the Study of Occupation monitoring, Mariupol, June 2025
notes: Head O. Makhankov; assessed as co-opting "marginalised far-left adolescents"; a youth ideological structure rather than a paramilitary training centre.

name: Espanola, Mariupol / «Эспаньола»
category: Adult formation recruiting youth
type: Adult paramilitary formation (focus on youth recruitment)
affiliation: Originates from an association of Russian football ultras
activity: Recruitment of marginalised young people into the formation
sources: Centre for the Study of Occupation monitoring, Mariupol, June 2025
notes: Differs in type from other entries: an adult armed formation included for its role in drawing in young people; to be marked separately from youth organisations proper.

name: Boevoe Bratstvo volunteer company, Mariupol / Добровольческая рота «Боевого братства»
category: Veterans' organisation
type: Youth-volunteer wing of a veterans' organisation
affiliation: All-Russian veterans' organisation Boevoe Bratstvo; works in tandem with the Young Guard of United Russia
legal_status: Company attached to the regional branch of Boevoe Bratstvo
activity: Searching for missing persons, distributing aid, camps, memorial events
sources: Centre for the Study of Occupation monitoring, Mariupol, June 2025
notes: Leaders A. Demydov (MGER) and S. Kuzmenko; curator D. Sablin (GRU); an example of structural rather than one-off involvement by a veterans' organisation (see the rule on veterans' organisations).

name: Krasnaya Gvozdika ("Red Carnation") camp, Zaporizhzhia oblast / Лагерь «Красная гвоздика»
category: Club, cadet corps or camp inside the territory
affiliation: Not established
activity: Not detailed; assessed as indoctrination of children in place without removal to Russia
participants: About 1,500 children in 2025 (double the previous year)
sources: TOT Insights, Education and Militarisation analytical brief, 2026
notes: No cross-tag: the camp operates inside the occupied territory and the child does not leave it (see the rule on camps).

name: Youth Golden Fund, Berdiansk / «Молодежный золотой фонд»
category: Youth movement or federal structure
type: Network and grant programme for youth activists
affiliation: Not established
activity: Building a pro-Russian cadre of youth leaders for "electoral", volunteer and campaigning events; linked to "tactical medicine and search detachments"
sources: Centre for the Study of Occupation monitoring, Zaporizhzhia oblast, June 2026
notes: Prepares young people for work with combat trauma and casualty evacuation.

name: Russian Orthodox Church paramilitary youth clubs (Orthodox Knights, Keepers of the Faith, Patriot and others)
category: Club, cadet corps or camp inside the territory
type: Network of religiously affiliated military-patriotic clubs
affiliation: Russian Orthodox Church
legal_status: Clubs and camps affiliated with the Russian Orthodox Church
activity: Tactical training, shooting and weapons handling combined with an ideology of "service to Russia"; the Brotherhood of Orthodox Pathfinders runs "Cadet Corps" camps (fortification, medicine; priests teach disassembly of the AK-74)
participants: At least 150 clubs and camps; about 25,000 minors a year
sources: TOT Insights, The Voin Generation (2026), citing Eastern Human Rights Group / ISRS data, September to October 2025
notes: The Church has also published the brochure "To Live Is to Serve the Motherland" and runs the Spas centre (Tambov) and Predtechenskiy Gorodok (Rostov).

name: Cossack youth paramilitary structures of Crimea (School of Young Atamans, Crimean Cossack Kurin, Crimean District Cossack Society, Bulat centre, Union of Paratroopers of Crimea)
category: Club, cadet corps or camp inside the territory
affiliation: Black Sea Cossack Host / state budgetary institution Cossacks of Crimea
locality: Crimean Federal University (Simferopol), Bilohirka village, Krasnoperekopsk
founded: Crimean Cossack Kurin, 2004; others not established
activity: Drill, shooting, sabre handling, tactical medicine, the game "Cossack Alarm"; a range and trenches at the Bulat centre
participants: 290 to 500 children per session (School of Young Atamans)
sources: "Universal Soldier" and monitoring reports of the Almenda centre, 2022 to 2025; Ukrainian Helsinki Human Rights Union / USAID, 2020
notes: Head of the School of Young Atamans: V. Motuzko.

name: Other military-patriotic clubs and field camps in Crimea and the south (Crimea Tactics, Gornyi camp, Selet-Ak Bars, Crimean Frontier camp, Preobrazhenskyi centre, ROKOT, Red Eagle, SKIL, DOSAAF Yalta / Arkhangel)
category: Club, cadet corps or camp inside the territory
type: Network of clubs and field camps (inside the territory)
affiliation: Not established
legal_status: Network of separate clubs and camps
activity: The programmes "Mountain Rifleman" and "Young Warrior" and the game "Shield and Sword" (shooting, tactics, drones); firearms, medical, engineering and CBRN training (Foros); training of drone operators, Arkhangel (Yalta)
sources: "Universal Soldier" and monitoring reports, including July to September 2025
notes: Instructors at Foros are the Heroes of Russia D. Polkovnikov and V. Nedobezhkin (see entry 5).

name: Amazonki club, Horlivka / ВПК «Амазонки»
category: Club, cadet corps or camp inside the territory
affiliation: Member of the Yunarmiya movement
founded: From the first years of the occupation of Donbas (2014 to 2015)
activity: Sniper training; participation in competitions in Moscow oblast
sources: Barbieri, Ethnopolitics 23(5), 2024, pp. 519 to 520
notes: Historical record, to 2019.

name: Vityaz club, Donetsk / ВПК «Витязь»
category: Club, cadet corps or camp inside the territory
affiliation: Member of the Yunarmiya movement
activity: Annual competitions at a military "college"; winners sent to a Russian "patriotic" camp; some members joined the "DNR" armed forces
sources: Barbieri, Ethnopolitics 23(5), 2024, pp. 519 to 520
notes: Head coach a former Russian officer and Afghanistan veteran.

name: Dobrovolets club, LNR / ВПК «Доброволец»
category: Club, cadet corps or camp inside the territory
affiliation: Not established
activity: The commander openly stated that the club trained recruits for the "republic's" security apparatus
sources: Barbieri, Ethnopolitics 23(5), 2024, p. 519

name: Berkut and Russkiy Medved clubs, Dokuchaievsk / ВПК «Беркут» и «Русский медведь»
category: Club, cadet corps or camp inside the territory
affiliation: Received "patriotism lessons" from the "DNR ministry of information"
activity: Master classes for schoolchildren in assembling and disassembling Kalashnikov rifles and hand-to-hand combat
sources: Barbieri, Ethnopolitics 23(5), 2024, pp. 521 to 522; Ukrainian Helsinki Human Rights Union / USAID, 2020, pp. 44 to 50
notes: The number of military-patriotic clubs in the "DNR" tripled between 2014 and 2019, to 62.

name: O. Grishin Association of Military-Patriotic Clubs / Patriotic Forces of Donbas
category: Club, cadet corps or camp inside the territory
affiliation: Initiated by O. Khodakovsky (commander of Vostok, former commander of the SBU's Crimean Alpha unit, former "DNR minister of state security")
activity: Preparing young people for entry to the military "colleges" of the "DNR" and "LNR"
sources: Barbieri, Ethnopolitics 23(5), 2024, p. 520
notes: Patriotic Forces of Donbas was later merged into the regular armed formations of the "DNR".

name: Vympel camp, DNR / Табір «Вымпел»
category: Club, cadet corps or camp inside the territory
type: Children's and youth military camp (historical, inside the territory)
affiliation: Vostok battalion
activity: Military and medical training, survival skills, weapons assembly; vehicle training by fighters of the Oplot battalion
participants: Children aged 10 to 17 from various "DNR" clubs
sources: Barbieri, Ethnopolitics 23(5), 2024, p. 520
notes: Oplot's commander was O. Zakharchenko, later "head of the DNR".

name: Lesnye Prostory camp, LNR / Табір «Лесные просторы»
category: Club, cadet corps or camp inside the territory
type: Children's and youth military camp (historical, inside the territory)
affiliation: Vernoe Kazachestvo / Patriotic Association of Donbas
activity: Annual "St George" military-patriotic rally; recruitment by officers of the "LNR interior ministry" for service in the security structures
sources: Barbieri, Ethnopolitics 23(5), 2024, pp. 520 to 521
notes: Became the model for other "LNR" camps.

name: Vernoe Kazachestvo and the Patriotic Association of Donbas, LNR / «Верное казачество» и «Патриотическая ассоциация Донбасса»
category: Club, cadet corps or camp inside the territory
affiliation: "Ministries" of internal affairs, emergencies and education of the "LNR"
activity: Running the "St George rally" at the Lesnye Prostory camp
sources: Barbieri, Ethnopolitics 23(5), 2024, p. 521
notes: Ataman: O. Selivanov.

name: A. Zakharchenko Cadet Corps, Donetsk School No. 4 / Кадетский корпус им. А. Захарченко
category: Club, cadet corps or camp inside the territory
type: Cadet corps (school; historical with current status)
affiliation: Personal initiative of O. Zakharchenko (first "DNR" leader)
activity: Weapons handling and elements of hand-to-hand combat from year 4 (in military uniform); meetings with veterans, participation in "Victory parades" (Moscow, Volgograd)
participants: About 200 children (as of 2024, including first-year pupils)
sources: Freedom House / ZMINA / Regional Centre for Human Rights / Viasna / BELPOL, "Stolen Childhood", October 2024, section 2.4 (pp. 17 to 19)
notes: In September 2022, 52 cadets aged 8 to 13 were taken to the Dubrava camp in Belarus. Cross-tag: Accountability and Legal (transfer of children).

name: Night Wolves, Luhansk chapter / Луганский осередок «Ночные волки»
category: Club, cadet corps or camp inside the territory
type: Motorcycle club / paramilitary formation (historical with current status)
affiliation: Registered as "LNR people's militia" under the "interior ministry"
activity: Mandate for patriotic education; a "war museum" for "cultivating the military-patriotic spirit of youth"
sources: Barbieri, Ethnopolitics 23(5), 2024, p. 522
notes: The club is personally linked to Putin.

name: Artek International Children's Centre, Hurzuf / «Артек»
category: Camp or centre moving children out of their territory
type: State children's centre (removal outside the territory of origin)
affiliation: Overseen by Russian deputy prime minister D. Chernyshenko
activity: Indoctrination and Russification of local youth and of young people brought from other occupied territories
sources: https://www.radiosvoboda.org/a/news-zelensky-sanktsii-artek/33439180.html
notes: Cross-tag: Accountability and Legal (the child leaves the territory of origin); Ukrainian presidential sanctions, 10 June 2025.

name: Luchistyi and Druzhba camps, Yevpatoria / Табори «Лучистый» і «Дружба»
category: Camp or centre moving children out of their territory
type: Children's "health" camps (removal of children from other occupied oblasts)
affiliation: Not established
territory: Crimea (receiving); Kherson oblast (origin of the children)
activity: Holding children, confiscating phones and cutting contact with families for "bad behaviour" or refusing to sing the Russian anthem; isolation ("punishment cell") of adolescents with pro-Ukrainian views
sources: Ukrainian Helsinki Human Rights Union / USAID, "Return of Deported Ukrainian Children by Their Parents", 2023, p. 24; Save Ukraine / War Child UK, "Return Every Child", 2025, pp. 24 to 25
notes: Cross-tag: Accountability and Legal (forced inter-oblast transfer of children within the occupied territories with the features of a deportation mechanism).

name: Russian Special Forces University, Gudermes, Chechnya, and the "Teenagers of Russia" programme
category: Camp or centre moving children out of their territory
affiliation: Decision of M. Lvova-Belova (Russian children's rights commissioner) and R. Kadyrov; curator "minister" A. Dudayev
territory: Donetsk and Luhansk oblasts (origin of the children); Chechnya (receiving)
founded: Not established (late 2022, the "Forces of the Caucasus" project)
activity: "Military-patriotic education": tours of the training ground, lectures on "heroes of Rosgvardia", weapons-handling training
participants: Stated aim of expanding to 1,000 adolescents; about 200 adolescents ("Forces of the Caucasus" project, late 2022)
sources: ZMINA, "Forced Transfer and Deportation to Russia of Children from the Occupied Territories of Ukraine", April 2023, p. 20; National Council of Ukraine on Television and Radio Broadcasting, analytical report 2023, pp. 23 and 28 to 29
notes: Cross-tag: Accountability and Legal (the child leaves the territory).

name: Smena centre, Krasnodar krai / Центр «Смена»
category: Camp or centre moving children out of their territory
affiliation: Russian Ministry of Education
territory: Four occupied oblasts (origin of the children)
activity: Building drones, mine detectors and magazine-loading devices for rifles; firearms training, tactical medicine, parachute training (for children from Donetsk oblast)
sources: Yale School of Public Health, Humanitarian Research Lab, report of 16 September 2025
notes: Cross-tag: Accountability and Legal (the child leaves the territory); part of the network of 210 facilities identified by Yale HRL.

name: "Children of Donbas" initiative, Snegiri, Moscow oblast / «Дети Донбасса»
category: Camp or centre moving children out of their territory
type: Programme for removing children to Russia
affiliation: Linked to the Russian State Duma; initiators L. Kalashnikov, G. Zyuganov, I. Kobzon
territory: Donetsk and Luhansk oblasts (origin of the children)
activity: "Rest from shelling" and integration of children at a holiday home
participants: About 16,000 children since 2015 (according to the organisers)
sources: National Council of Ukraine on Television and Radio Broadcasting, analytical report 2023, pp. 12 to 13
notes: Cross-tag: Accountability and Legal (the child leaves the territory); the initiators are sanctioned for this activity.

name: Sirius educational centre, Sochi / «Сириус»
category: Camp or centre moving children out of their territory
affiliation: Office of the Russian children's rights commissioner
activity: "Integration sessions" under the guise of "career guidance and moral support"; in practice re-education and adaptation "to life in a new country"
sources: National Council of Ukraine on Television and Radio Broadcasting, analytical report 2023, p. 23
notes: Cross-tag: Accountability and Legal (the child leaves the territory).

name: Cadet and Cossack classes and corps in the occupied territories (network)
category: Curriculum programme
affiliation: Patrons: Rosgvardia, FSB, Russian Investigative Committee, Emergencies Ministry, Interior Ministry, sometimes the Ministry of Defence; Cossack classes under the Crimean Cossack District
locality: Crimea (109 rising to 244 classes in 78 schools), LNR (86 cadet and 62 Cossack classes), Zaporizhzhia oblast (11 to 13), Kherson oblast (8 to 9), Mariupol (School No. 28), Luhansk (Luhansk Cossack Cadet Corps)
legal_status: Network of school classes and corps within general education institutions
funding: State budget and departmental funding (Rosgvardia, Investigative Committee, Emergencies Ministry, Interior Ministry)
activity: Drill, hand-to-hand combat, weapons handling and shooting within the school curriculum; apex institutions are the Crimean Cadet Corps (53% of graduates go on to the universities of Russia's security ministries), the Mariupol branch of the Nakhimov Naval School (560 places) and the Sevastopol Presidential Cadet School
sources: Crimean Human Rights House / Crimean Human Rights Group / Regional Centre for Human Rights / Almenda / ZMINA, 2021, pp. 63 to 65; Crimean Human Rights Group, 12 June 2020, https://crimeahrg.org/uk/rosijske-kadetstvo-zamist-krimskogo-ditinstva/; Save Ukraine / War Child UK, 2025
notes: Type: curriculum programme or structure; no membership or premises outside the school network.

name: "Anti-terror schools", Mariupol Schools No. 14 and No. 59 / «Школы антитеррора»
category: Curriculum programme
affiliation: Civil defence corps of Moscow oblast
activity: Shaping a perception of Ukrainians as a "terrorist threat", building barricades; standing "rescue detachments" as institutionalised children's paramilitary groups
sources: TOT Insights, Education and Militarisation analytical brief, section 2.4
notes: Type: curriculum programme.

name: OBZR, "Fundamentals of Security and Defence of the Motherland" (school subject) / ОБЗР
category: Curriculum programme
affiliation: Russian Ministry of Education
locality: All schools in the occupied territories
founded: Updated programme approved January 2026; a separate pre-conscription training programme in Crimea, November 2022
activity: Building and piloting drones (about 90 units of equipment); compulsory field camps for years 8 and 10 at military training grounds
participants: Not stated (covers all pupils in the relevant years)
sources: Russian Ministry of Education programme document on basic military training for years 10 to 11; TOT Insights, Education and Militarisation analytical brief, section 2.4; TOT Insights, The Voin Generation (2026), section II
notes: Type: curriculum programme; replaced and expanded the former "Fundamentals of Life Safety".

name: Zarnitsa 2.0 military-sports game / «Зарница 2.0»
category: Curriculum programme
affiliation: Movement of the First jointly with Yunarmiya and the Voin centre; family format with the Defenders of the Fatherland foundation
locality: Mariupol, Zaporizhzhia oblast, Kherson oblast and elsewhere
founded: Not established (timed to the "anniversary of the liberation of Donbas")
activity: Garrison duty, tactical exercises, mastering specialisms (medic, sapper, drone operator, war correspondent); disciplines include rifle disassembly, air-rifle shooting, drone piloting, drill and firearms training
participants: Mariupol: over 2,600 children (first half of 2025); Zaporizhzhia oblast: over 2,000 planned
sources: Centre for the Study of Occupation monitoring, Mariupol and Luhansk oblast, 2025, and Mariupol, June 2026
notes: The Vulkan-7 team (Kherson region) reached the final in Volgograd oblast; type: curriculum and extracurricular programme.

name: Yunarmiya House, drone and tactical-medicine training, Mariupol School No. 26, and the Berloga programme / «Дом Юнармии» + «Берлога»
category: Curriculum programme
affiliation: Yunarmiya; the Berloga programme is approved by Putin
territory: Donetsk oblast (Mariupol); drone training across the occupied territories
founded: Not established (grant of 1.2 million roubles in 2025)
legal_status: Structure based at a general school
funding: Regional grant (1.2 million roubles, 2025) plus state budget
activity: Shooting, knife throwing, sapper work, weapons assembly and disassembly, drone piloting (FPV drones: aerodynamics, modelling, piloting); tactical medicine as a school subject
participants: About 10,000 adolescents involved in practical drone-operator training programmes
sources: Centre for the Study of Occupation monitoring, Mariupol, June 2026, section 11; TOT Insights, The Voin Generation (2026), sections II and V
notes: Berloga is integrated into Zarnitsa and the Movement of the First ("Pilots of the Future" competition); separate classes for children with disabilities.

name: Ideological lessons: "Conversations about What Matters", "Lessons of Courage", "Hero's Desk", "Spiritual and Moral Culture of Russia"
category: Curriculum programme
affiliation: Russian Ministry of Education; the subject was developed with the participation of Metropolitan Tikhon Shevkunov
locality: All schools and, from October 2024, kindergartens in the occupied territories
founded: September 2022 (launch of "Conversations about What Matters"); October 2024 (extended to kindergartens from age 5); 2025/26 school year, an "adviser on upbringing" post in every school in occupied Kherson oblast
activity: Justifying the war, portraying Russia as a "peacemaker" and Ukrainian resistance as "Nazism"; "lessons of courage" with invited veterans; war museums and "Hero's Desks" in schools; "Alleys of Glory" with busts of killed occupation soldiers
participants: Not stated (covers all pupils in the occupied territories)
sources: Centre for the Study of Occupation monitoring, Donetsk and Luhansk oblasts and Mariupol, 2025 to 2026; National Council of Ukraine on Television and Radio Broadcasting, analytical report 2023
notes: Type: curriculum programme; the widest coverage of any entry in the dataset (all schoolchildren in the occupied territories).
